decisions.rationale: 'Friedreich ataxia' names one specific disease with no further categorization, so it is a Specific Disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Annotate all Specific Disease mentions

decisions.rationale: This is a second occurrence of the same specific disease name in the same sentence. Duplicate mentions are annotated separately.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 4: Annotate duplicate mentions

decisions.rationale: 'FRDA' is the abbreviation defined in '( FRDA )' for Friedreich ataxia. Abbreviation definitions are split into separate mentions, and this short form is annotated as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 6: Annotate all synonymous mentions (abbreviation definitions)

decisions.rationale: 'neurodegenerative disease' refers to a family of multiple specific diseases rather than one defined disease, so it is a Disease Class. The generic word 'disease' alone would be excluded, but this compound describes a category.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Disease Class definition

decisions.rationale: Here 'FRDA' is used as part of the genetic locus order 'cen-FRDA-D9S5-D9S15-qter' and refers to the locus position rather than to the disease itself. It is therefore a disease name used as a modifier of a non-disease concept.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'FRDA' modifies the noun 'locus' ('the FRDA locus') and refers to the genetic locus, not the disease, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'FRDA' modifies 'families' ('available FRDA families'), denoting patient families that are used as a modifier of another noun phrase.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'FRDA' is used as a modifier in 'close FRDA flanking markers' and refers to the locus context of the markers, so it is a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'FRDA' is used as a standalone reference point for marker position ('proximal to FRDA') denoting the locus. It is not the disease itself, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'FRDA' modifies 'locus' ('the FRDA locus') and refers to the genetic locus being placed in an interval, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts
